extraction.name: SWE-rebench
extraction.description: A public dataset of interactive Python-based software engineering tasks mined automatically from GitHub repositories. It is designed for training and benchmarking software engineering agents, with decontaminated evaluation support via a related benchmark and leaderboard.
extraction.creator: Ibragim Badertdinov, Alexander Golubev, Maksim Nekrashevich, Anton Shevtsov, Simon Karasik, Andrei Andriushchenko, Maria Trofimova, Daria Litvintseva, Boris Yangel
extraction.rai:dataCollection: An automated pipeline processed a large volume of raw data through several stages to curate the final SWE-rebench dataset.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Human annotations were used to predict three quality assessment labels: Test Patch Correctness, Task Complexity, and Issue Clarity.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: A classification quality report was provided comparing a vanilla model and a fine-tuned model on a validation set, with precision, recall, F1, and accuracy reported.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: A fine-tuned Qwen 2.5-72B-Instruct model was used to predict annotation labels.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The initial release is limited exclusively to Python, which restricts applicability to other language ecosystems; the automated pipeline also relies on heuristics and LLM-driven interpretations, which may introduce errors and reduce quality.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The fully automated pipeline may produce tasks that are imperfectly described or unsolvable solely from the issue, and the automated quality assessment cannot fully replicate nuanced human judgment, which can lower absolute success rates compared to manually curated benchmarks. The initial release is limited to Python.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The benchmark may support transparency and standardization in evaluating SWE agents, but it may also accelerate increasingly autonomous AI systems in software engineering, with risks including overreliance on AI-generated code and misuse of automated agents for introducing vulnerabilities.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Designed for agent-based training and benchmarking/evaluating SWE agents; intended to support transparency and standardization in evaluation. The release is decontaminated and aimed at fresh, up-to-date benchmark tasks.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The pipeline is intended to provide a continual supply of fresh data, and support for additional languages is planned for future work; no explicit versioning or deprecation policy is stated.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Automated pipeline processes raw data through several stages to curate the final dataset; includes dependency installation and filtering to issue-linked PRs / Python projects.
